_: The life packages. A new one is ONE line in 'packages' plus its own files (assets/life-<id>.js, optionally assets/life-<id>.css); nothing else is edited. id: the package's name (its elements carry data-life-for="<id>"). surface: the pages it runs on, from chrome (every page), home, select, story, library, people, worlds. js, css: files in assets/. cost: css | waapi | webgl | physx (what the work is, for the budget's ladder). label: what it honestly is: PhysX | custom force on PhysX | spring/ODE | shader | CSS. priority: higher stays longer when the page is slow (the lowest goes first). needs: ['physx'] or ['webgl'] (the package is only mounted where the gate allows it; physx also makes the build embed the physics configuration). min: the lowest effects tier it runs on: lite (CSS and Web Animations, phones included), rich or ultra. debug: true, it runs only with ?fxdebug=1. A package exports mount(ctx) (or a default function) and may return { dispose() }. deps: files the package loads itself (a module, an atlas), handed to it hashed as ctx.deps in this order. max: the highest tier it runs on (a fallback that stands down where the real thing runs). It is never mounted for reduced motion, Light mode or Save-Data.
